title: Monetary Policy Report – July 2018
summary: The Federal Reserve's July 2018 Monetary Policy Report to Congress documented a strengthening labor market with average payroll gains of 215,000/month in H1 2018, pushing the unemployment rate down to 4.0% from 4.1% in December 2017. The report noted the unemployment rate had fallen below all FOMC participants' estimates of its longer-run normal level and was near the lows last reached in 2000. Labor force participation held steady at 62.9% amid an aging population, while the employment-to-population ratio rose to 60.4%, reflecting both falling unemployment and improving participation among prime-age workers.
key_points: Total nonfarm payroll employment averaged 215,000/month in H1 2018, up from 2017 pace and well above what is needed for new labor force entrants
Unemployment rate declined from 4.1% in December 2017 to 4.0% in June 2018, below all FOMC participants' longer-run normal estimates
Labor force participation rate (LFPR) held at 62.9% in June, little changed since late 2013, with aging population offset by rising prime-age participation
Employment-to-population ratio reached 60.4% in June, gradually increasing since 2011
Job openings, quits rate, and hiring all remained elevated; layoff rate and initial unemployment claims near multi-decade lows
Involuntary part-time employment fell further and is now close to pre-recession levels
why_it_matters: The why_it_matters states this report informed 'market expectations for the pace of monetary tightening' and markets used it 'to calibrate Fed policy expectations and positioning ahead of the September 2018 FOMC meeting.' These claims are plausible inferences but cannot be verified against the visible source since Part 2 (Monetary Policy) is truncated. Consider softening to note this was the Fed's official economic assessment as of mid-2018.
macro_context: The macro_context claims the FOMC statement noted 'economic risks are roughly balanced' at the July 31-August 1 meeting. This statement cannot be verified from the visible source since Part 2 is not available. Human reviewer should verify this claim or remove the specific language.
important_numbers: 215,000/month - average payroll job gains in H1 2018
62.9% - labor force participation rate in June 2018
